answer: Each agent must lock a deposit of scarce timber before it can submit bids, then earn it back only after completing a task that a randomly selected peer verifies against the work itself. A trellis of cross-checks limits how often the same peers can verify one another, so an attacker cannot cheaply mint identities and rubber-stamp them into a trusted cluster. Failed or colluding reviews forfeit the deposit; the fable of a convincing profile is not enough. Sybils therefore require real capital, sustained useful work, and exposure to slashing.
